items.claim: Value change while disabled marks the field dirty against a baseline equal to that value
items.consequence: A controlled control rendered disabled while data loads (disabled={loading} value={value}) is unregistered, so its baseline is captured only when it is enabled, at the already-loaded value. The value change during loading still runs the new useValueChanged effect, which compares against the empty initialValue and latches data-dirty (and markedDirtyRef). The field then reads dirty with the loaded value as its baseline; typing and returning to the loaded value clears it, confirming the baseline was the loaded value all along. The adversarial reviewer reproduced this with a scratch test.
items.proposed_fix: Skip the dirty/validation sync until the control has registered a baseline (e.g. only run the effect body when enabled, or compare against a baseline set synchronously in captureInitialValue). Assumption: a value change before the baseline exists should become the baseline, not count as an edit.

items.claim: PR description and code disagree: processedValueRef, focus-latch fix and cancel semantics are not in the diff
items.consequence: The description promises that a control that unmounts or becomes disabled while focused no longer latches data-focused, that a processedValueRef guards double validation, that details.cancel() stops internal handling, and that clearErrors is not called on programmatic change. The diff has no focus cleanup and no processedValueRef (grep finds none). The controlled path returns before the isCanceled check and the value-change effect validates regardless, so cancel() combined with a consumer that still sets state still runs validate (reproduced by the adversarial reviewer). The effect also calls clearErrors(name), contradicting the Open question. Reviewers and consumers will assume behavior that is not shipped, and the focus latch remains.
items.proposed_fix: Either add the described behavior (setFocused(false) when the control is disabled or unmounts while focused; honor details.isCanceled on the controlled echo path) or remove those claims from the PR description. Also correct the Open question: the diff does call clearErrors(name) in the value-change effect.

residual_risks: Programmatic value changes now call clearErrors(name): a consumer that resets or trims the value after a server error silently drops the Form server error for that field.
Form-submit validation (registration.value) and validate now receive the String()-serialized controlled value rather than the raw number/array, a behavior change for controlled non-string values.
Async-loaded controlled data (value starts empty, then loads) now reads dirty and, with validationMode=onChange, runs validate on load, since the baseline is the first registered value.
Controlled path no longer honors event.nativeEvent.defaultPrevented; a consumer that preventDefaults and still sets state validates via the echo.
testing_gaps: No test for a controlled Field.Control that is disabled when its value changes (baseline vs dirty).
No test for data-focused when a focused control becomes disabled or unmounts, despite the PR claiming a fix.
